question: Under Wis. Stat. 709.001(5), what does "real property" mean for purposes of the Chapter 709 disclosure requirements?
choice_a: Any real property regardless of the number of dwelling units or whether it has ever been inhabited
choice_b: Real property that includes 1 to 4 dwelling units and has been inhabited, or real property that does not include any buildings
choice_c: Only real property with 5 or more dwelling units
choice_d: Only commercial real property that includes no dwelling units
explanation: Sec. 709.001(5) defines "real property" as either property that includes 1 to 4 dwelling units (excluding property that has not been inhabited) or property that does not include any buildings (vacant land).

question: Under Wis. Stat. 709.001(4), how is the term "qualified 3rd party" defined for purposes of Chapter 709?
choice_a: It has the meaning given in Wis. Stat. 452.25(1)(d)
choice_b: It is defined independently within Chapter 709 and does not cross-reference Chapter 452
choice_c: It has the meaning given in Wis. Stat. 452.23(2)(b)
choice_d: It means only a licensed professional engineer
explanation: Sec. 709.001(4) provides that "qualified 3rd party" has the meaning given in s. 452.23(2)(b), tying the owner-disclosure chapter's terminology to the licensee-disclosure statute.

question: Under Wis. Stat. 709.001(6), the definition of "time-share property" used in Chapter 709 is drawn from which other statute?
explanation: Sec. 709.001(6) states that "time-share property" has the meaning given in s. 707.02(32). By contrast, "unit"/"condominium unit" is drawn from 703.02(15), "dwelling unit" from 101.61(1), and "public agency" from 66.0825(3)(h).

question: Under Wis. Stat. 709.01(1), which types of property transfers trigger the obligation to comply with the Chapter 709 disclosure requirements?
choice_a: Transfers of real property in Wisconsin, including a condominium unit or time-share property, by sale, exchange, or land contract, unless the transfer is exempt from the real estate transfer fee under s. 77.25
choice_b: Only transfers by warranty deed for a purchase price over $50,000
choice_c: Only transfers that close within 30 days of contract acceptance
choice_d: Any transfer of personal property located on real estate
explanation: Sec. 709.01(1) requires compliance with ss. 709.02 to 709.04 and 709.06 for transfers of real property (including condominium units and time-share property) by sale, exchange, or land contract, unless the transfer is exempt from the real estate transfer fee under s. 77.25.

question: Under Wis. Stat. 709.01(2), a personal representative, trustee, conservator, or court-appointed fiduciary is excused from the Chapter 709 disclosure requirement only if which additional condition is also met?
choice_a: The person has held the property for less than one year
choice_b: The person has never occupied the property being transferred
choice_c: The sale price is below the property's assessed value
choice_d: The buyer waives the requirement in writing before closing
explanation: Sec. 709.01(2) excuses personal representatives, trustees, conservators, and court-appointed/court-supervised fiduciaries from sub. (1) only "if those persons have never occupied the property transferred."

question: Under Wis. Stat. 709.02(1), by when must an owner furnish a completed condition report to a prospective buyer?
choice_a: Not later than 10 days before the closing date
choice_b: Not later than 30 days after the listing agreement is signed
choice_c: Not later than 10 days after acceptance of a contract of sale or option contract
choice_d: At the time the property is first listed for sale
explanation: Sec. 709.02(1) requires the owner to furnish a completed copy of the report under s. 709.03 or 709.033, whichever is applicable, "not later than 10 days after acceptance of a contract of sale or option contract."

question: A seller signs (accepts) an offer to purchase on Day 0 but never furnishes a real estate condition report to the buyer. Under Wis. Stat. 709.02(1), what is the buyer's remedy, and by when must the buyer act?
choice_a: The buyer has no remedy and must proceed to closing regardless
choice_b: The buyer may only sue the seller for money damages equal to the cost of an inspection
choice_c: The buyer may rescind at any time up until the day of closing, with no outer deadline
choice_d: The buyer may rescind the contract in writing within 2 business days after the end of the 10-day period for furnishing the report, and is entitled to return of any deposits or option fees
explanation: Sec. 709.02(1) gives a prospective buyer who does not receive the report within the 10-day period the right to rescind, within 2 business days after the end of that 10-day period, by delivering written notice to the owner or the owner's agent, and to recover any deposits or option fees paid.

question: Under Wis. Stat. 709.02(1), when is a real estate condition report under s. 709.03 or 709.033 considered "complete"?
choice_a: Only if the owner answered, or supplied information under s. 709.035 for, each item on the report
choice_b: As soon as the owner signs the certification, regardless of whether any items were left blank
choice_c: Only after a licensed home inspector co-signs the report
choice_d: As soon as the buyer acknowledges receipt of the report, regardless of its content
explanation: Sec. 709.02(1) provides that a report is "considered complete only if the owner answered, or supplied information under s. 709.035 for, each item on the report."

question: Under Wis. Stat. 709.02(1), an owner may substitute information supplied by certain professionals for an entry on the condition report. Which of the following is one of the listed categories whose written, timely, identified information the owner may substitute?
choice_a: Any friend or family member of the owner who has visited the property
choice_b: A licensed engineer, professional land surveyor, structural pest control operator, a qualified 3rd party, or a contractor about matters within the contractor's occupation, as well as information supplied by a public agency
choice_c: The buyer's own home inspector, regardless of who retained that inspector
choice_d: Only a licensed real estate broker representing the owner
explanation: Sec. 709.02(1) allows the owner to substitute written, timely, identified information from a licensed engineer, professional land surveyor (s. 443.01(7m)), structural pest control operator, an individual who is a qualified 3rd party, or a contractor (about matters within the contractor's occupation), and separately allows substitution of information supplied by a public agency.

question: Under Wis. Stat. 709.02(2), when a transfer involves a condominium unit, what must the owner furnish in addition to and at the same time as the report required under sub. (1)?
choice_a: Nothing additional; the standard residential report under s. 709.03 fully satisfies condominium transfers
choice_b: Only a copy of the condominium's most recent property tax bill
choice_c: An addendum with the condominium's name and creation date, unit number and seller contact information, association information and management status, current assessments/fees and payment status, and (unless excused) a copy of the executive summary required under s. 703.33(1)(h)
choice_d: A separate appraisal of the condominium unit performed within the prior 90 days
explanation: Sec. 709.02(2) requires an addendum covering the condominium's name/creation date, unit number and seller/agent contact info; association name, address, management status, and representative contact; current assessments, fees, special assessments, and payment status; and, unless excused by s. 703.365(8), a copy of the executive summary required under s. 703.33(1)(h).

question: According to the disclaimer language prescribed by Wis. Stat. 709.03 for the Real Estate Condition Report, what is the report NOT intended to be?
choice_a: A legally binding contract between the buyer and seller
choice_b: Admissible evidence in any later dispute concerning the property
choice_c: A public record once filed with the register of deeds
choice_d: A warranty of any kind by the owner or any agents representing any party, and not a substitute for any inspections or warranties the parties may wish to obtain
explanation: The statutory disclaimer in s. 709.03 states the report "IS NOT A WARRANTY OF ANY KIND BY THE OWNER OR ANY AGENTS ... AND IS NOT A SUBSTITUTE FOR ANY INSPECTIONS OR WARRANTIES THAT THE PARTIES MAY WISH TO OBTAIN."

question: The statutory Real Estate Condition Report form under Wis. Stat. 709.03 includes a "Notice to Parties Regarding Advice or Inspections." What does that notice say real estate licensees may NOT do?
choice_a: Provide advice or opinions concerning whether an item is a defect for purposes of the report, or concerning the legal rights or obligations of the parties to the transaction
choice_b: Show the property to prospective buyers without the owner's written consent
choice_c: Attend the property inspection alongside the buyer's inspector
choice_d: Communicate with the buyer's attorney at any point during the transaction
explanation: The form's notice states that "[r]eal estate licensees may not provide advice or opinions concerning whether or not an item is a defect for the purposes of this report or concerning the legal rights or obligations of parties to a transaction."
source_note: Wis. Stat. 709.03 (RECR form, Notice to Parties Regarding Advice or Inspections)

question: On the statutory Real Estate Condition Report form (Wis. Stat. 709.03, item A1), how is the term "aware" defined?
choice_a: The owner(s) have been formally certified as experts on the condition described
choice_b: The owner(s) have notice or knowledge
choice_c: A licensed inspector has confirmed the condition in writing
choice_d: The condition is visible without the aid of any tool or instrument
explanation: Item A1 of the form defines "aware" to mean the "owner(s)" have notice or knowledge.

question: On the statutory Real Estate Condition Report form (Wis. Stat. 709.03, item A2), which of the following correctly states the three-part definition of "defect"?
choice_a: Any condition that the owner personally considers unattractive, regardless of its effect on value, safety, or the property's expected life
choice_b: Only a condition that violates a specific building code section identified by a municipal inspector
choice_c: A condition that would have a significant adverse effect on the value of the property; that would significantly impair the health or safety of future occupants; or that, if not repaired, removed, or replaced, would significantly shorten or adversely affect the expected normal life of the premises
choice_d: Only a condition that would cost more than $5,000 to repair
explanation: Item A2 defines "defect" using the three-part test: significant adverse effect on value; significant impairment of the health or safety of future occupants; or, if unrepaired, significant shortening or adverse effect on the expected normal life of the premises.

question: Under item A4 of the statutory Real Estate Condition Report form (Wis. Stat. 709.03), what must the owner do if the owner answers any question on the form "yes"?
choice_a: Immediately withdraw the property from the market
choice_b: Obtain a licensed contractor's repair estimate before the report can be furnished
choice_c: Notify the Department of Safety and Professional Services in writing
choice_d: Provide, in the additional information area of the form, an explanation of the reason why the response is "yes"
explanation: Item A4 states that if the owner responds to any question with "yes," the owner shall provide, in the additional information area of the form, an explanation of the reason why the response is "yes."

question: Item B2 of the statutory Real Estate Condition Report form (Wis. Stat. 709.03) asks about defects in the electrical system. Which of the following is listed as an example of such a defect?
choice_a: Knob and tube wiring, 60 amp service, or aluminum-branch circuit wiring
choice_b: The presence of a smart thermostat
choice_c: A recently replaced circuit breaker panel installed under permit
choice_d: The use of copper wiring throughout the home
explanation: Item B2's guidance text lists electrical wiring not in compliance with applicable code, knob and tube wiring, 60 amp service, or aluminum-branch circuit wiring as example electrical defects.

question: Item B6 of the statutory Real Estate Condition Report form (Wis. Stat. 709.03) includes a note about state law requirements for detectors. What does that note say?
choice_a: State law requires only a single smoke detector anywhere in the home, with no carbon monoxide detector requirement
choice_b: State law requires operating smoke detectors on all levels of all residential properties, and operating carbon monoxide detectors on all levels of most residential properties
choice_c: Detector requirements under state law apply only to rental properties, not owner-occupied homes
choice_d: State law leaves detector requirements entirely to local municipalities, with no statewide floor
explanation: Item B6's note states that state law requires operating smoke detectors on all levels of all residential properties and operating carbon monoxide detectors on all levels of most residential properties, citing Wis. Stat. ch. 101.
source_note: Wis. Stat. 709.03 (RECR form, item B6, citing ch. 101)

question: Item C2 of the statutory Real Estate Condition Report form (Wis. Stat. 709.03) carries a note about a federal disclosure requirement for certain older homes. What does that note address?
choice_a: A federal asbestos abatement mandate applicable to any home built before 1990
choice_b: A federal requirement to test private wells for radon before every residential sale
choice_c: Specific federal lead paint disclosure requirements that must be complied with in the sale of most residential properties built before 1978
choice_d: A federal mandate requiring flood insurance on any home located within one mile of a river
explanation: Item C2's note states: "Specific federal lead paint disclosure requirements must be complied with in the sale of most residential properties built before 1978."
source_note: Wis. Stat. 709.03 (RECR form, item C2 note)

question: Item D1 of the statutory Real Estate Condition Report form (Wis. Stat. 709.03) covers well defects. Which of the following is listed as an example of a well water defect?
choice_a: Water that is simply harder or softer than the buyer prefers
choice_b: A well that produces slightly more water pressure than average
choice_c: A well that was drilled more than 25 years before the sale
choice_d: Unsafe levels of bacteria (total coliform and E. coli), nitrate, or arsenic affecting human consumption safety
explanation: Item D1's guidance text lists unsafe levels of bacteria (total coliform and E. coli), nitrate, arsenic, or other substances affecting human consumption safety as example well water defects.

question: Item D6 of the statutory Real Estate Condition Report form (Wis. Stat. 709.03) asks about underground or aboveground fuel storage tanks. What does the form note about an owner who answers "yes"?
choice_a: The owner, by law, may have to register the tanks with the Wisconsin Department of Agriculture, Trade and Consumer Protection, whether the tanks are in use or not, and DATCP regulations may require closure or removal of unused tanks
choice_b: The owner must immediately excavate and remove the tank before the report can be furnished
choice_c: The tank must be registered with the Wisconsin Department of Natural Resources within 24 hours of contract acceptance
choice_d: No registration or regulatory consequence attaches to a "yes" answer on this item
explanation: Item D6 notes that if the answer is "yes," the owner may by law have to register the tanks with DATCP (P.O. Box 8911, Madison, WI 53708) whether in use or not, and that DATCP regulations may require closure or removal of unused tanks.

question: Item E3m, newly added to the statutory Real Estate Condition Report form (Wis. Stat. 709.03), asks about an "existing neighborhood improvement special assessment." When does this form item take effect, and under what act was it created?
choice_a: Effective immediately upon the original 1991 enactment of Chapter 709
choice_b: Effective October 1, 2026, created by 2025 Wisconsin Act 120
choice_c: Effective January 1, 2020, created by 2019 Wisconsin Act 1
choice_d: It has no specified effective date and applies retroactively to all past transfers
explanation: The statutory text includes the note "(Form) E3m. is created eff. 10-1-26 by 2025 Wis. Act 120," adding a question about existing neighborhood improvement special assessments to the E. Taxes, Special Assessments, Permits, Etc. section.
source_note: hedge: very recently enacted (2025 Wis. Act 120), effective 10-1-2026, per docs.legis.wisconsin.gov as published 8-5-2026; verify current form version before relying on this item's presence at time of use

question: Item F10 of the statutory Real Estate Condition Report form (Wis. Stat. 709.03) addresses use-value assessment of agricultural land. Under Wis. Stat. 74.485(2), what may a person owe upon converting agricultural land assessed at use value to a nonagricultural use?
choice_a: An automatic doubling of that year's property tax bill with no separate charge
choice_b: A mandatory donation to the county's farmland preservation fund
choice_c: A use-value assessment conversion charge
choice_d: Nothing; use-value assessment status carries no conversion consequence under Wisconsin law
explanation: Item F10 explains that converting agricultural land assessed under the use-value system (s. 70.32(2r)) to a nonagricultural use may trigger a use-value assessment conversion charge under s. 74.485(2), which may also be deferred under s. 74.485(4).
source_note: Wis. Stat. 709.03 (RECR form, item F10, citing 70.32(2r) and 74.485)

question: Item F11 of the statutory Real Estate Condition Report form (Wis. Stat. 709.03) addresses farmland preservation agreements. What conversion fee can early termination of, or removal of land from, such an agreement trigger?
choice_a: A flat conversion fee of $500 regardless of the land's value
choice_b: No conversion fee; farmland preservation agreements may be terminated at will with no financial consequence
choice_c: A conversion fee equal to the land's full fair market value
choice_d: A conversion fee equal to 3 times the class 1 "use value" of the land
explanation: Item F11 states that early termination of a farmland preservation agreement, or removal of land from such an agreement, can trigger payment of a conversion fee equal to 3 times the class 1 "use value" of the land.

question: Item F19 of the statutory Real Estate Condition Report form (Wis. Stat. 709.03) addresses a property abutting the bed of a navigable waterway owned by a hydroelectric operator. Under Wis. Stat. 30.132, what may such an owner be required to do before placing a structure on the bed of the waterway?
choice_a: Ask the permission of the hydroelectric operator
choice_b: Obtain a federal permit from the Army Corps of Engineers only, with no state-level requirement
choice_c: Nothing; owners abutting such waterways have unrestricted rights to build on the waterway bed
choice_d: Pay a one-time state riparian development tax
explanation: Item F19 notes that under s. 30.132, the owner of a property abutting the bed of a navigable waterway owned by a hydroelectric operator (as defined in s. 30.132(1)(b)) may be required to ask the permission of the hydroelectric operator to place a structure on the bed of the waterway.
source_note: Wis. Stat. 709.03 (RECR form, item F19, citing 30.132)

question: Item G1 of the statutory Real Estate Condition Report form (Wis. Stat. 709.03) asks the owner about insurance claims. What time period does this question cover?
choice_a: Whether the owner has ever filed an insurance claim on the property, with no time limitation
choice_b: Whether the owner has filed any insurance claims relating to damage to the property or premises within the last five years
choice_c: Whether the owner has filed an insurance claim within the last 90 days only
choice_d: Whether the owner's insurer has ever denied a claim on the property
explanation: Item G1 asks: "Have you filed any insurance claims relating to damage to this property or premises within the last five years?"

question: Item G4 of the statutory Real Estate Condition Report form (Wis. Stat. 709.03) asks whether the owner is a "foreign person" as defined in 26 USC 1445(f). What federal law does this question relate to, and what does it generally require of the buyer?
choice_a: The federal Fair Housing Act, which requires the buyer to certify their citizenship before closing
choice_b: The federal RESPA statute, which requires the buyer to pay all foreign sellers in U.S. currency only
choice_c: The Foreign Investment in Real Property Tax Act (FIRPTA), under which a buyer of a U.S. real property interest must be notified in writing and must withhold tax if the seller is a foreign person, unless an exception applies
choice_d: A federal law that bars foreign persons from owning U.S. residential real estate outright
explanation: Item G4's explanatory note identifies 26 USC 1445 as FIRPTA and explains that a transferee (buyer) of a U.S. real property interest must be notified in writing and must withhold tax if the transferor (seller) is a foreign person, unless a FIRPTA exception applies.
source_note: Wis. Stat. 709.03 (RECR form, item G4, citing 26 USC 1445)

question: Item F20 of the statutory Real Estate Condition Report form (Wis. Stat. 709.03) asks whether the owner is aware of one or more burial sites on the property. Which organization does the form direct owners and buyers to contact for information about burial sites?
choice_a: The Wisconsin Department of Natural Resources
choice_b: The Real Estate Examining Board
choice_c: The county register of deeds
choice_d: The Wisconsin Historical Society
explanation: Item F20 directs parties with questions about the presence, preservation, and potential disturbance of burial sites to contact the Wisconsin Historical Society.

question: Item F7 of the statutory Real Estate Condition Report form (Wis. Stat. 709.03) asks about restrictive covenants or deed restrictions. Which example does the form itself give of a program that can create such a restriction?
choice_a: A development that received Infrastructure Access or Vacancy-to-Vitality funds from the Wisconsin Housing and Economic Development Authority (WHEDA)
choice_b: A development financed entirely through a conventional 30-year fixed-rate mortgage
choice_c: A property enrolled only in the standard homestead property tax credit
choice_d: A property that has never had a homeowners association
explanation: Item F7's guidance text gives, as an example, a development that received Infrastructure Access or Vacancy-to-Vitality funds from WHEDA, which can carry resale price limits, occupancy requirements, or other time-limited restrictions.

question: Comparing the residential Real Estate Condition Report under Wis. Stat. 709.03 to the vacant land disclosure report under Wis. Stat. 709.033, which section is present in the residential form but absent from the vacant land form?
choice_a: A section addressing environmental hazards
choice_b: Section B, "Structural and Mechanical"
choice_c: A section addressing wells, septic systems, and storage tanks
choice_d: A section addressing land use
explanation: The residential form under s. 709.03 begins with section B, "Structural and Mechanical," covering the roof, electrical, plumbing, HVAC, etc. The vacant land form under s. 709.033, which applies to property with no buildings, has no such structural/mechanical section and instead begins its lettered sections with B, "Environmental."
source_note: Wis. Stat. 709.03 vs. 709.033 (RECR form structure comparison)

question: Item B4 of the vacant land disclosure report form (Wis. Stat. 709.033) asks about subsoil conditions that would significantly increase development costs. Which of the following is listed as an example of such a subsoil condition?
choice_a: The presence of decorative landscaping rock on the surface
choice_b: Soil that has recently been professionally graded and compacted to code
choice_c: High groundwater, or adverse soil conditions such as low load-bearing capacity, earth or soil movement, settling, upheavals, or slides
choice_d: A soil composition ideal for residential foundation construction
explanation: Item B4 lists examples including subsurface foundations or waste material, fill, contaminated dumpsites, high groundwater, adverse soil conditions (low load-bearing capacity, earth or soil movement, settling, upheavals, or slides), and excessive rocks or rock formations.
source_note: Wis. Stat. 709.033 (vacant land form, item B4)

question: Item B6 of the vacant land disclosure report form (Wis. Stat. 709.033) asks about "brownfields" or other contaminated land. Which of the following cleanup programs does the item specifically cite as relevant to this question?
choice_a: Only the federal Superfund program, with no reference to any Wisconsin-specific program
choice_b: The Wisconsin Homestead Tax Credit program
choice_c: The Wisconsin Managed Forest Law program
choice_d: The Petroleum Environmental Cleanup Fund Act (PECFA), a DNR remedial or cleanup program, or the DATCP Agricultural Chemical Cleanup Program
explanation: Item B6 defines brownfields as abandoned, idled, or underused land that may be subject to environmental contamination and asks whether contaminated soils have been cleaned up under PECFA, a DNR remedial or cleanup program, the DATCP Agricultural Chemical Cleanup Program, or a similar program.
source_note: Wis. Stat. 709.033 (vacant land form, item B6)

question: Item F6 of the vacant land disclosure report form (Wis. Stat. 709.033) asks about utility connections. Which of the following utilities does this item specifically list?
choice_a: Electricity, municipal water, telephone, cable television, natural gas, and municipal sewer
choice_b: Only electricity and municipal water, with no other utilities addressed
choice_c: Satellite internet and cellular signal strength
choice_d: Only natural gas and propane delivery service
explanation: Item F6 asks whether the property is connected, on the property or at the lot line, to electricity, municipal water, telephone, cable television, natural gas, and municipal sewer, and if so, where the utility is located.
source_note: Wis. Stat. 709.033 (vacant land form, item F6)

question: Item E22 of the vacant land disclosure report form (Wis. Stat. 709.033) addresses the managed forest land program. For how long do orders designating land as managed forest land generally remain in effect?
choice_a: 5 or 10 years
choice_b: 25 or 50 years
choice_c: Indefinitely, with no fixed term
choice_d: 1 year, renewable annually
explanation: Item E22 states that orders designating lands as managed forest lands remain in effect for 25 or 50 years, and that a new owner of enrolled land must file a change-of-ownership report with DNR and pay a fee to continue compliance with the program.
source_note: Wis. Stat. 709.033 (vacant land form, item E22)

question: Item E20 of the vacant land disclosure report form (Wis. Stat. 709.033) groups several distinct disclosure topics into a single question. Which group of items does this question ask about together?
choice_a: Only zoning code violations
choice_b: Only the presence of a homeowners association
choice_c: Archeological artifacts, mineral rights, orchards, or endangered species on the property
choice_d: Only water quality issues relating to lead
explanation: Item E20 asks in a single question: "Are you aware of archeological artifacts, mineral rights, orchards, or endangered species on the property?"
source_note: Wis. Stat. 709.033 (vacant land form, item E20)

question: Item E21 of the vacant land disclosure report form (Wis. Stat. 709.033) asks about a specific type of agricultural structure. What does this item ask about?
choice_a: The presence of a working grain elevator on the property
choice_b: Whether the property has ever hosted a farmers' market
choice_c: Whether livestock is currently being raised on the property
choice_d: Existing or abandoned manure storage facilities located on the property
explanation: Item E21 asks: "Are you aware of existing or abandoned manure storage facilities located on the property?"
source_note: Wis. Stat. 709.033 (vacant land form, item E21)

question: Under Wis. Stat. 709.035, if an owner learns of new information that would change a report response before a contract of sale or option contract is accepted, what five items must the resulting amendment or amended report state?
choice_a: The address of the property, the owner's name, the date of the report being amended, the number of the affected statement, and how the original response is changed (with an explanation if changed to "yes")
choice_b: Only the buyer's name and the closing date
choice_c: Only a general narrative of what changed, with no specific statement number required
choice_d: The property's legal description and the names of all licensees involved in the transaction
explanation: Sec. 709.035(1)-(5) requires the amendment to state the property address, the owner's name, the date of the report being amended, the number of the affected statement, and how the original response is changed, including an explanation if the new response is "yes."

question: Under Wis. Stat. 709.035, an owner discovers new information affecting a report response. Within what timeframe, and relative to what event, must the owner submit the amendment?
choice_a: At any point up until the day before closing, with no earlier deadline
choice_b: Before acceptance of a contract of sale or option contract, and within the time required under s. 709.02
choice_c: Only if the buyer specifically requests an update in writing
choice_d: Within 30 days after the buyer moves into the property
explanation: Sec. 709.035 applies when the owner obtains the new information "before acceptance of a contract of sale or option contract," and requires the owner to submit the amendment "within the time required under s. 709.02."

question: Under Wis. Stat. 709.04, how must an owner indicate compliance with Chapter 709's disclosure requirements?
choice_a: By recording a separate compliance affidavit with the register of deeds
choice_b: By filing a compliance certificate with the Real Estate Examining Board
choice_c: On the contract of sale or option contract, on the closing statement, or in an addendum to one of those documents
choice_d: Compliance need not be indicated anywhere; furnishing the report itself is the only requirement
explanation: Sec. 709.04 requires the owner to indicate compliance with Chapter 709 on the contract of sale or option contract, on the closing statement, or in an addendum to one of those documents.

question: Under Wis. Stat. 709.05(1), if a buyer receives a condition report after submitting a contract of sale, and the report discloses a defect, what right does the buyer have?
choice_a: The buyer must renegotiate price but may not rescind the contract
choice_b: The buyer may only recover the cost of repairing the disclosed defect
choice_c: The buyer has no right to act on the disclosure once the contract is signed
choice_d: The buyer may rescind the contract in writing before the applicable deadline, without liability, and is entitled to the return of any deposits or option fees paid
explanation: Sec. 709.05(1) gives a buyer who receives a report disclosing a defect, after submitting the contract, the right to rescind in writing before the applicable deadline without liability, with entitlement to return of deposits or option fees.

question: Under Wis. Stat. 709.05(1), a buyer receives a report that is incomplete or that inaccurately asserts an item is "not applicable," and the buyer is not aware of the undisclosed defects. Within what timeframe may the buyer rescind?
choice_a: Within 2 business days after receipt of that report
choice_b: Within 30 calendar days after receipt of that report
choice_c: At any time before closing, with no specific outer limit
choice_d: Within 2 business days after the closing date
explanation: Sec. 709.05(1) allows a buyer who receives an incomplete report, or one with an inaccurate "not applicable" assertion, and who is unaware of the undisclosed defects, to rescind in writing within 2 business days after receipt of that report.

question: Under Wis. Stat. 709.05(2)(a)1., what is the general rule if a buyer receives a complete condition report before submitting the contract of sale or option contract to the owner or the owner's agent?
choice_a: The buyer automatically has an unlimited right to rescind at any time before closing
choice_b: The buyer may not rescind the contract under s. 709.05, except as provided for a later amended report disclosing a new defect
choice_c: The report is void and must be re-furnished after contract submission
choice_d: The 10-day disclosure deadline under s. 709.02 no longer applies
explanation: Sec. 709.05(2)(a)1. provides that, except as provided in subd. 2. (the amended-report exception), a buyer may not rescind under s. 709.05 if the buyer received a complete report before submitting the contract of sale or option contract.

question: Under Wis. Stat. 709.05(2)(a)2., what exception allows a buyer who already received a complete report before submitting the contract to still rescind?
choice_a: The buyer may rescind for any reason within 24 hours of signing, regardless of the report's content
choice_b: There is no such exception; subd. 1.'s bar on rescission is absolute
choice_c: If, after submitting the contract, the buyer receives an amended report or amendment disclosing a defect that was not disclosed in the report previously received, the buyer may rescind after receipt and before the applicable deadline
choice_d: The buyer may rescind only if the seller agrees in writing to accept the rescission
explanation: Sec. 709.05(2)(a)2. creates an exception: if the buyer later receives an amended report or amendment disclosing a defect not previously disclosed, the buyer may, after receipt and before the applicable deadline, rescind and recover deposits or option fees (subject to par. (b)).

question: Under Wis. Stat. 709.05(2)(b), when is a buyer barred from rescinding a contract based on a defect disclosed in a report, amended report, or amendment to a report?
choice_a: Whenever the defect relates to the roof or foundation specifically
choice_b: Whenever the purchase price is below the property's assessed value
choice_c: The buyer is never barred from rescinding once any defect is disclosed
choice_d: If the buyer was aware, or had written notice, of the nature and extent of the defect at the time the contract of sale or option contract was submitted to the owner or the owner's agent
explanation: Sec. 709.05(2)(b) bars rescission on the basis of a defect if the buyer was already aware of, or had written notice of, the nature and extent of that defect when the contract was submitted to the owner or the owner's agent.

question: Under Wis. Stat. 709.05(3), a rescission is considered timely if delivered to the owner or the owner's agent within what period?
choice_a: 2 business days after the prospective buyer or the buyer's agent receives the report, amended report, or amendment to the report
choice_b: 5 calendar days after the report is signed by the owner
choice_c: 10 business days after the closing date
choice_d: Any time before the deed is recorded, with no specific window
explanation: Sec. 709.05(3) states that rescissions under this section are timely if delivered within 2 business days after the prospective buyer or the buyer's agent receives the report, amended report, or amendment to the report.

question: Under Wis. Stat. 709.05(4), what is the status of the right to rescind established by that section relative to other remedies under Chapter 709?
choice_a: It is merely one of several available remedies, alongside a statutory damages claim
choice_b: The right to rescind under s. 709.05 is the only remedy under Chapter 709
choice_c: It applies only if the buyer also proves the owner acted in bad faith
choice_d: It is available only to commercial buyers, not individual buyers
explanation: Sec. 709.05(4) states plainly: "The right to rescind under this section is the only remedy under this chapter."

question: Under Wis. Stat. 709.06, what standard governs an owner's performance of the acts and disclosures required by Chapter 709?
choice_a: The owner is held to the same reasonably-prudent-licensee standard applied to real estate licensees under s. 452.23(4)
choice_b: The owner is held to a strict-liability standard regardless of honesty or knowledge
choice_c: The owner shall perform each act, and make each disclosure, required by this chapter with honesty in fact
choice_d: The owner need only substantially comply, with no honesty requirement specified
explanation: Sec. 709.06, titled "Good faith," states that the owner shall perform each act and make each disclosure required by Chapter 709 "with honesty in fact" -- a distinct, owner-specific standard from the reasonably-prudent-licensee standard that s. 452.23(4) applies to real estate licensees.

question: Under Wis. Stat. 709.07, when is an owner NOT liable for an error or omission in a condition report under s. 709.03 or 709.033?
choice_a: Whenever the buyer had the opportunity to obtain an independent inspection but declined to do so
choice_b: Whenever the error or omission is discovered more than one year after closing
choice_c: Only if the owner obtained a signed liability waiver from the buyer at closing
choice_d: If the owner had no knowledge of the error or omission and it was based on information provided by a public agency, a licensed engineer, professional land surveyor, structural pest control operator, or qualified 3rd party, or by a contractor about matters within the contractor's occupation
explanation: Sec. 709.07 precludes owner liability for an error or omission the owner had no knowledge of, where the error or omission was based on information from a public agency, licensed engineer, professional land surveyor, structural pest control operator, qualified 3rd party, or a contractor about matters within the contractor's occupation.

question: Under Wis. Stat. 709.08, which of the following statements about waiver is accurate?
choice_a: A buyer may waive in writing the right to rescind under s. 709.05, and may separately waive in writing the right to receive the report required under s. 709.02; also, proceeding to closing terminates the buyer's right to rescind under s. 709.05
choice_b: Waivers under Chapter 709 are effective only if notarized and recorded with the register of deeds
choice_c: A buyer may waive the right to receive the report, but can never waive the right to rescind once a report is furnished
choice_d: Only the owner, not the buyer, may waive rights under Chapter 709
explanation: Sec. 709.08 allows a buyer to waive in writing the right to rescind under s. 709.05, provides that proceeding to closing terminates that rescission right, and separately allows the buyer to waive in writing the right to receive the report required under s. 709.02.

question: A buyer signs an offer that the owner accepts, then proceeds all the way through closing without ever rescinding. Under Wis. Stat. 709.08, what is the legal effect of proceeding to closing on the buyer's rescission right under s. 709.05?
choice_a: The right to rescind survives closing indefinitely unless separately waived in writing
choice_b: The buyer's right to rescind under s. 709.05 is terminated upon proceeding to closing
choice_c: Proceeding to closing has no effect on the rescission right one way or the other
choice_d: The right to rescind converts automatically into a right to sue for damages after closing
explanation: Sec. 709.08 states: "If a buyer proceeds to closing, the buyer's right to rescind under s. 709.05 is terminated."

question: Item B10 of the statutory Real Estate Condition Report form (Wis. Stat. 709.03) asks about rented items. Which example does the item give of a rented item that must be disclosed?
choice_a: A rented moving truck used on the day of closing
choice_b: Furniture the seller plans to remove before closing
choice_c: A water softener or other water conditioner system, or other items affixed to or closely associated with the property
choice_d: A rental car used by the owner during the listing period
explanation: Item B10 asks whether the owner is aware of rented items located on the property such as a water softener or other water conditioner system, or other items affixed to or closely associated with the property.

question: Item C4 of the statutory Real Estate Condition Report form (Wis. Stat. 709.03) asks about hazardous or toxic substances. What is distinctive about the location covered by this particular item, compared with item C2?
choice_a: Item C4 asks only about substances stored inside the home's garage
choice_b: Item C4 duplicates item C2 exactly, with no distinction in scope
choice_c: Item C4 applies only to commercial properties, never to residential property
choice_d: Item C4 asks about unsafe concentrations, unsafe conditions, or storage of hazardous or toxic substances on neighboring properties, whereas C2 asks about hazards on the subject property itself
explanation: Item C4 specifically asks about the presence of, or a defect caused by, unsafe concentrations of, unsafe conditions relating to, or the storage of hazardous or toxic substances on neighboring properties, distinguishing it from item C2's focus on hazards located on the subject property.

question: Item F9 of the statutory Real Estate Condition Report form (Wis. Stat. 709.03) asks about a DNR-related mitigation plan. What does this item ask the owner to disclose?
choice_a: Whether the property is subject to a mitigation plan required under DNR administrative rules related to county shoreland zoning ordinances, obligating the owner to establish or maintain shoreland-condition measures, and enforceable by the county
choice_b: Whether the property has ever been used for a DNR-sponsored fishing tournament
choice_c: Whether the owner has applied for a DNR hunting permit for the property
choice_d: Whether the property contains a state-designated snowmobile trail
explanation: Item F9 asks whether the owner is aware of the property being subject to a mitigation plan required under DNR administrative rules related to county shoreland zoning ordinances, which obligates the owner to establish or maintain certain shoreland-condition measures and is enforceable by the county.

question: Item F14 of the statutory Real Estate Condition Report form (Wis. Stat. 709.03) addresses boundary or lot line disputes, encroachments, or encumbrances. Which specific example is expressly named in the item's introductory question itself (not just the guidance text)?
choice_a: An underground fuel storage tank
choice_b: A joint driveway
choice_c: A conservation easement
choice_d: A homeowners association assessment
explanation: Item F14's question text itself reads: "Are you aware of boundary or lot line disputes, encroachments, or encumbrances (including a joint driveway) affecting the property?" -- naming a joint driveway directly in the question.
